subject: SLA headroom variance request — uptime & latency-tier exceptions
messages:
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@novascale.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jul 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA template + headroom variance for initial ramp

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at NovaScale is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the routing options. Procurement asked me to send our ask in writing so legal can start parallel review. High level:

- We need an explicit allowance for a temporary uptime headroom during our initial production ramp (month 1–3) due to predictable warm-up/batching behavior with our workloads.
- We also want a clearer monthly credit mechanism tied to uptime bands and a carveout for scheduled maintenance and autoscaling-induced transient spikes.
- Finally, latency SLOs (p95/p99) will be a requirement for our customer-facing flows; we need to understand how credit triggers tie to latency degradations as well as availability.

Can you send your standard SLA template and flag any sections where Redwood would be flexible on the uptime floor, credit cap, or latency-triggered credits? I attached a short security questionnaire procurement wanted answered as well.

Attaching: NovaScale_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Erin Cole
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaScale Systems

From: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@novascale.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 06 Jul 2025 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA template + headroom variance for initial ramp

Erin —

Appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire. Looping in Laura (sales) and Marcus (contracts) so we can respond with an authoritative template and proposed carveouts. Quick context from our side: Redwood's hosted standard is 99.95% monthly uptime with a per-month credit ladder that scales as uptime decreases (we typically cap credits at 50% of the monthly invoice for hosted plans). We do make limited exception paths for pilot/ramp phases where customers need explicit "headroom" for warm-up behavior.

What I'll do next:
- Share our SLA_Template_v1.pdf that highlights uptime bands, credit calculation, maintenance carveouts, and latency SLO language.
- Propose an initial pilot variance that reduces the baseline to 99.9% for months 1–3 with a scaled credit cap (we can discuss percent).
- Call out latency-triggered credit mechanics: we calculate latency credits separately on a p95/p99 basis for critical routes; those credits do not stack with availability credits (we provide the higher of the two).

Marcus — can you confirm appetite to offer a temporary headroom (99.9%) and a reduced cap (30% of monthly invoice) for a three-month ramp, with a maintenance graceband of up to 4 hours/month excluded? Laura, happy to sync with Erin on timing.

Attachments: SLA_Template_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@novascale.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA template + headroom variance for initial ramp

Diego / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the template. We reviewed the SLA and have an internal counter-proposal:

- NovaScale cannot accept a 50% credit cap even as a starting point; we need either no cap during the pilot or a much higher cap (recommendation: uncapped for months 1–3) because our procurement team has commitments to our customers if Redwood's service is degraded.
- The proposed separate latency-credit non-stacking approach is reasonable, but we need clearer thresholds: can you specify numeric SLOs and the exact credit percentages tied to p95/p99 tiers?
- The 4-hour maintenance graceband is acceptable only if maintenance windows are scheduled and limited to off-peak PST hours; otherwise we need to limit the carveout to 2 hours/month.

I've attached our redline doc (NS-Proposal-SLA-Comments.docx) with inline comments. Legal also asked for a DocuSign redline pathway so we can expedite once we converge on terms.

Attaching: NS-Proposal-SLA-Comments.docx

Regards,
Erin Cole
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaScale Systems

Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2025 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA template + headroom variance for initial ramp — Redwood counter

Erin —

Thanks for the detailed redlines. After a quick internal review with Marcus and our legal team, here's a proposed middle path that should address NovaScale's operational risk while keeping our commercial exposure bounded: 

1) Uptime baseline & pilot headroom
- Months 1–3: Temporary baseline set to 99.90% monthly uptime (down from 99.95%).
- Months 4+: Revert to standard 99.95% baseline.

2) Monthly credit cap
- Pilot months (1–3): Credit cap of up to 30% of the monthly invoice.
- Post-pilot: Standard cap of 50% remains.

3) Maintenance graceband
- Excluded maintenance window: up to 4 hours/month during pilot, provided maintenance is scheduled 72 hours in advance and occurs between 1:00 AM–5:00 AM PST. If maintenance falls outside those windows and impacts production, that time counts toward uptime calculations.

4) Latency-tier SLOs & credits
- We propose explicit numeric SLOs for the critical customer-facing route you flagged: p95 < 200 ms, p99 < 450 ms (measured at our edge).
- Credit triggers: if p95 breaches the threshold for more than 15% of observability sampling in a month, we calculate a latency credit equal to the availability credit for the equivalent degradation band. Latency and availability credits are reconciled so the customer receives the higher single credit per month (they do not stack).

5) Process & next steps
- If this direction is acceptable, we'll prepare an SLA redline and route via DocuSign (link below) for legal review. We can also run a one-week shadow run where NovaScale's traffic is mirrored to our pilot pool to validate warm-up behavior prior to month 1 billing.

DocuSign route: https://docusign.net/link/NS-0042-SLA
Drive folder with redlines: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cSLA-comments

Let me know if you want Marcus and I to join a 30-minute call with your legal/procurement to walk through the specific language. Happy to be flexible on the cap and SLO numeric thresholds as long as we have shared observability and a defined pilot window.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
